chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Ismail ibn al-Khaliq, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time of the Dhuhr prayer, so he said: 'After the sun has passed its zenith by a hand's breadth or thereabouts, except on Friday or during travel, for its time is when the sun passes its zenith.'

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Solar zenith (the moment the sun passes its highest point)
key_terms.بِقَدَمٍ: By a hand's breadth (a small measure of time)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Dhuhr prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the preferred time (*waqt al-fadila*) and the essential time (*waqt al-darura*) for Dhuhr, noting that while a slight delay is generally recommended, Friday prayers and those of travelers commence immediately at solar zenith. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (*rukha*) granted to travelers and the specific emphasis on Friday, reflecting the practical considerations of communal worship and ease in Islamic law.
